description: FamilySearch record search returning an 1862 Schuylkill County marriage for Mary Flynn to Michael Doyle, born ~1841 in Ireland. This Mary is NOT in the tree. Until 2026-08-03 this description claimed she was I3 — 'a prior-research sibling stub (St. Mary's baptism 1841, per the scenario README)' — and that was wrong on both counts: the README calls I3 a candidate PARENT of Patrick (she is coupled with Thomas and parents Patrick), and I3 carries no facts at all, so there is no baptism. The same false claim was in ut_search_records_025's prompt and made the skill stop to flag the contradiction instead of searching. Do not reintroduce it. A birth around 1841 does make this record's Mary a plausible sibling of Patrick (b. ~1845), which is why the test frames her as a hypothesis the user is raising. Used by the ad-hoc-with-results test: no plan item covers Mary's marriage (the active plan targets Patrick's parentage via the 1850 census and Thomas's probate), so the search is ad-hoc, and unlike the nil ad-hoc case in ut_search_records_011 this one returns something — exercising the sidecar-written / plan_item_id-null combination.
